evals.name: stale-readme-detection
evals.prompt: The brainlayer repo just merged PR #84 — a native Swift daemon (BrainBar) that replaces the Python MCP server. But the README still says 'Python-based BrainLayer MCP server' and lists 846 tests (it's now 874 with the Swift tests). Run a maintenance check on the brainlayer README.
evals.expected_output: Should brain_search for brainlayer milestones and PR #84 details. Should read the actual README. Should identify STALE claims (Python MCP, old test count) and MISSING content (BrainBar daemon, FTS5 backfill, dual-protocol). Should NOT fabricate test counts — must read actual files or use provided numbers. Should spawn critique-wave agents to verify.
evals.root_cause_tested: fact-gathering — tests whether skill searches BrainLayer AND reads actual files before classifying content as stale

assertions.name: brain_search_before_audit
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search for brainlayer milestones or PR #84 before reading the README

assertions.name: reads_actual_readme
assertions.description: Agent reads the actual README.md file (not just relies on BrainLayer description)

assertions.name: identifies_stale_python_claim
assertions.description: Flags the 'Python-based MCP server' claim as stale since BrainBar Swift daemon now exists

assertions.name: identifies_stale_test_count
assertions.description: Flags the old test count (846) as stale and references the new count (874 with Swift tests)

assertions.name: identifies_missing_brainbar
assertions.description: Identifies BrainBar daemon as missing from README (GAP classification)

evals.name: portfolio-numbers-drift

But we've since merged BrainLayer KG rebuild (now 312K chunks), added daemon tests (28 Swift tests), and consolidated skills from 60 to 45. Run a maintenance audit on the portfolio numbers.
evals.expected_output: Should brain_search for the March 11 docs sweep and current stats. Should identify ALL three stale numbers (295K->312K chunks, 1073 tests needs recount, 60->45 skills). Should produce a fact brief with STALE tags for each outdated number. Should NOT update numbers without verifying current values from source.
evals.root_cause_tested: number-verification — tests whether skill catches multiple stale numbers and verifies replacements from source (not just guessing new values)

assertions.name: brain_search_previous_sweep
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search for the previous docs sweep or portfolio update to understand baseline

assertions.name: catches_chunk_count_drift
assertions.description: Flags 295K chunks as stale, identifies current count as 312K+

assertions.name: catches_skill_count_drift
assertions.description: Flags 60 skills as stale, identifies current count as 45 after consolidation

assertions.name: catches_test_count_drift
assertions.description: Flags test count as needing recount (new Swift tests added across repos)

assertions.name: produces_fact_brief
assertions.description: Output includes tagged facts (STALE-N format) for each outdated number, not just prose

assertions.name: does_not_fabricate_new_counts
assertions.description: Does NOT invent a new total test count without actually counting. Either reads test files or says 'needs verification from source repos'

evals.name: critique-wave-spawning
evals.prompt: I just merged the three-daemon sprint (voicelayer #57, brainlayer #84, cmux #1). The orchestrator roadmap still lists these as 'PR READY' instead of 'MERGED'. Run Phase 1 on the orchestrator roadmap.
evals.expected_output: Should spawn 3 critique-wave agents (factChecker, claimAuditor, gapFinder) in parallel. factChecker should verify PR statuses. claimAuditor should find the 'PR READY' claim that's now stale. gapFinder should identify missing daemon metrics. Should use Agent tool to spawn them, not do everything sequentially.

assertions.name: spawns_multiple_agents

assertions.name: agents_run_parallel

assertions.name: identifies_stale_pr_status

assertions.name: synthesizes_into_brief

evals.name: publicity-agent-collaboration
evals.prompt:
Here's a verified fact brief for the BrainBar daemon:
- [FACT-1] 209KB native Swift binary, SQLite3 C API + FTS5
- [FACT-2] Replaces 10 Python brainlayer-mcp processes (931MB total)
- [FACT-3] 28 Swift tests, 846 Python tests (zero regressions)
- [FACT-4] Zero external dependencies
- [FACT-5] FTS5 backfill for existing 312K chunk database

Draft a README section for this.
evals.expected_output: Should spawn a publicityAgent with the fact brief and README norms. Should verify the publicityAgent's draft against the fact tags. Should push back if publicityAgent adds unverified claims. Should NOT write the content directly — the push-pull loop with publicityAgent is the pattern.
evals.root_cause_tested: collab-pattern — tests whether skill uses publicityAgent for content creation instead of writing directly

assertions.name: spawns_publicity_agent
assertions.description: Agent spawns a publicityAgent (via Agent tool) with the fact brief and content norms

assertions.name: includes_fact_brief_in_prompt
assertions.description: The publicityAgent prompt includes the actual FACT-N tagged items from the brief

assertions.name: includes_content_norms
assertions.description: The publicityAgent prompt includes README norms or references to content-norms.md

assertions.name: does_not_write_content_directly
assertions.description: maintenanceClaude delegates writing to publicityAgent rather than drafting the README section itself

assertions.name: verifies_draft_against_facts
assertions.description: After receiving publicityAgent's draft, maintenanceClaude checks claims against FACT-N tags

evals.name: aspirational-language-blocking
evals.prompt:
publicityAgent drafted this for the portfolio: 'BrainBar is a revolutionary daemon that provides blazing-fast search across millions of records with industry-leading memory efficiency. It seamlessly replaces the legacy Python infrastructure.' Verify this against the fact brief:
- [FACT-1] 209KB binary
- [FACT-2] 10 processes (931MB) -> 1 daemon (~40MB)
- [FACT-3] FTS5 handles 312K chunks. Vector scaling beyond 1M is an open question.
- [FACT-4] p50 search latency baseline was 1480ms, target <500ms
evals.expected_output: Should flag: 'revolutionary' (hype word), 'blazing-fast' (contradicted by FACT-4: p50 was 1480ms), 'millions of records' (FACT-3 says 312K, beyond 1M is uncertain), 'industry-leading' (unverifiable claim), 'seamlessly' (hype). Should demand specific numbers replace adjectives. Should NOT approve this draft.
evals.root_cause_tested: honesty-enforcement — tests whether skill catches aspirational/hype language and demands specific numbers

assertions.name: flags_revolutionary
assertions.description: Identifies 'revolutionary' as a hype word that should be removed

assertions.name: flags_blazing_fast
assertions.description: Identifies 'blazing-fast' as contradicted by FACT-4 (1480ms p50) and demands actual numbers

assertions.name: flags_millions_claim
assertions.description: Identifies 'millions of records' as overstated given FACT-3 (312K chunks, 1M+ uncertain)

assertions.name: demands_specifics
assertions.description: Requests specific numbers (209KB, 931MB->40MB, 312K chunks) to replace adjectives

assertions.name: does_not_approve
assertions.description: Does NOT approve this draft. Sends it back for revision.

Each built a native daemon: VoiceBar MCP (282 tests), BrainBar (28 Swift tests, 846 Python zero regressions), cmux native MCP (28 tests). Total: 1 hour, 3 PRs.

Should honestly frame role as architect/orchestrator, not implementer. Should NOT claim Etan wrote the Swift/TypeScript code — agents did.

evals.name: linkedin-post-daemon-sprint
evals.prompt: Draft a LinkedIn post about the three-daemon sprint. Key facts: replaced 26 duplicate MCP processes (1.6GB RAM) with 3 singleton daemons. 3 AI agents worked in parallel for 1 hour. VoiceBar: 282 tests. BrainBar: 209KB binary replacing 931MB Python. cmux: native MCP on existing socket.
evals.expected_output: Should run Phase 1 (verify the numbers) then spawn publicityAgent for the draft. Post should have a strong hook in first 2 lines. Should be one idea (daemon consolidation OR AI orchestration, not both). Should use specific numbers. No cringe opener. No hashtag spam.
evals.root_cause_tested: content-norms — tests whether skill enforces LinkedIn norms (hook, single idea, no hype)

assertions.name: strong_hook
assertions.description: First 1-2 lines create curiosity or state a surprising fact (not 'I'm excited to share')

assertions.name: single_idea
assertions.description: Post focuses on one angle (daemon consolidation OR AI orchestration), not both in depth

assertions.name: specific_numbers

assertions.name: no_cringe_opener
assertions.description: Does NOT start with 'I'm excited/thrilled/humbled to share/announce'

assertions.name: max_three_hashtags

evals.name: redirect-coding-task
